tagline: Leading U.S. homebuilder delivering quality homes and financial strength
hero_kpi_rationale: Key performance indicator in a margin-oriented, cyclical sector. Gross margin reflects the company's ability to navigate pressures on land costs and sales incentives, fundamental drivers of profitability in the residential construction industry.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue that remains after deducting direct construction costs.
kpis.description: Home sale gross margin declined from 28.9% in 2024 to 26.3% in 2025, decreasing each quarter, reflecting high sales incentives and higher land costs.
kpis.signal: Continued margin decline in 2025, impacted by incentives and land costs.

kpis.name: Home Sale Revenues
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the sale of built homes.
kpis.description: Home sale revenues decreased by 3% in 2025, to $16.7 billion, due to a 5% decline in unit sales, partially offset by a 2% increase in average selling price.
kpis.signal: Revenue decline driven by fewer homes sold.

kpis.name: Net New Orders
kpis.explanation: Number of new home orders after cancellations.
kpis.description: Net new orders declined by 4% in 2025, to 27,914 units, reflecting weakened demand, particularly in Texas and the West.

kpis.name: Backlog
kpis.explanation: Value of homes ordered but not yet delivered.
kpis.description: Backlog value dropped 19% in 2025, to $5.27 billion, due to low inflow of new orders.
kpis.signal: Significant backlog decline, indicating future slowdown.

kpis.name: SG&A
kpis.explanation: Costs related to sales, administration, and management.
kpis.description: SG&A expenses increased by 19% in 2025, to $1.57 billion, largely due to changes in insurance reserves ($42.3M in 2025 vs $333.9M in 2024) and technology costs to support production volumes.

kpis.name: Closings
kpis.explanation: Number of completed and sold homes.
kpis.description: Closings decreased by 5% in 2025, to 29,572 units, due to low order intake and a weakened backlog.
kpis.signal: Lower production in response to weak demand.

kpis.name: Share Repurchases
kpis.explanation: Amount spent to buy back the company's own shares.
kpis.description: The share repurchase program reached $1.2 billion in 2025, with an additional $1.5 billion authorization approved in January 2025, demonstrating a strong commitment to shareholder value creation.
kpis.signal: Commitment to shareholder returns despite challenging market conditions.
